dishes.make_ahead: First fry and smash up to 4 hours ahead, make the mojo up to 1 day ahead; do the second fry just before serving

steps.text: Peel the plantains by slitting the skin lengthways and prising it off, then cut into 3cm pieces.
Heat 3cm of the vegetable oil in a heavy pot to 160C.
Fry the plantain in batches until pale gold but still soft inside, then drain.
Smash each piece flat to about 1cm with the base of a glass.
Crush the garlic to a paste with half the salt, then stir in the olive oil, lime juice and coriander.
Turn the oil up to 180C and fry the smashed plantain again until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper towel, sprinkle with the rest of the salt and serve hot with the mojo.

dishes.n: Jets' corner cart hot dogs with onion sauce
dishes.make_ahead: Onion sauce up to 3 days ahead in the fridge, reheat with a splash of water; simmer the frankfurts to order

steps.text: Halve and thinly slice the onions.
Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat until soft and pale gold.
Stir in the tomato paste, chilli powder, cinnamon, sugar, vinegar and water and simmer until thick and jammy.
Simmer the frankfurts in a pot of barely bubbling water until hot through.
Warm the rolls in a low oven.
Tuck a frankfurt in each roll, spread with mustard and spoon over the onion sauce.

veg.n: Jets' corner cart hot dogs with onion sauce (vegetarian)
veg.make_ahead: Onion sauce up to 3 days ahead in the fridge, reheat with a splash of water; brown the sausages to order

steps.text: Halve and thinly slice the onions.
Cook the onions in 2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat until soft and pale gold.
Stir in the tomato paste, chilli powder, cinnamon, sugar, vinegar and water and simmer until thick and jammy.
Brown the vegetarian sausages in the rest of the oil in a frying pan, turning, until hot through.
Warm the rolls in a low oven.
Tuck a sausage in each roll, spread with mustard and spoon over the onion sauce.

dishes.n: Maria's pernil with arroz con gandules
dishes.make_ahead: Marinate the pork overnight, up to 1 day ahead, in the fridge; roast and make the rice on the day

ingredients.item: bunch coriander, stalks chopped, leaves picked

steps.text: Blend the garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, pepper, 60ml of the olive oil, the lime juice and orange juice to a paste.
Score the pork skin, rub the paste all over and into the cuts, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.
Take the pork out of the fridge to come to room temperature and heat the oven to 160C.
Roast skin up for 4 hours, then turn the oven to 230C for 25 minutes to crackle the skin.
While it roasts, soften the onion, capsicum and coriander stalks in the rest of the oil, then stir in the tomato paste, turmeric and rice for 2 minutes.
Add the pigeon peas, olives and stock, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Rest the pork 15 minutes, pull into chunks with the crackling and serve over the rice with coriander leaves and lime wedges.

veg.n: Maria's pernil-spiced cauliflower with arroz con gandules
veg.make_ahead: Rub the cauliflower and marinate up to 1 day ahead in the fridge; roast and make the rice on the day

ingredients.item: bunch coriander, stalks chopped, leaves picked

steps.text: Blend the garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, pepper, 70ml of the olive oil, the lime juice and orange juice to a paste.
Sit the whole cauliflowers in a roasting dish, rub the paste all over and into the florets, cover and marinate in the fridge for 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 200C.
Pour 125ml water into the dish, cover with foil and roast for 40 minutes, then uncover, baste and roast 30 minutes more until charred and tender.
While it roasts, soften the onion, capsicum and coriander stalks in the rest of the oil, then stir in the tomato paste, turmeric and rice for 2 minutes.
Add the pigeon peas, olives and stock, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Cut the cauliflowers into thick wedges and serve over the rice with the pan juices, coriander leaves and lime wedges.

dishes.n: Officer Krupke's corned beef and cabbage
dishes.make_ahead: Cook the beef up to 2 days ahead; reheat sliced in the cooking liquid

steps.text: Cover the beef with water, add the onion, peppercorns, sugar and vinegar and simmer gently.
Add the carrots and potatoes for the last part of cooking.
Steam the cabbage wedges until tender and toss with butter.
Slice the beef and serve with the vegetables and mustard.

veg.n: Officer Krupke's smoked tofu and cabbage
veg.make_ahead: Cook the tofu up to 2 days ahead; reheat sliced in the cooking liquid

steps.text: Simmer the potatoes and carrots in the stock with the onion, peppercorns and sugar until tender.
Warm the tofu in the stock for the last few minutes.
Steam the cabbage wedges until tender and toss with butter.
Serve the tofu with the vegetables and mustard.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake and chill up to 2 days ahead, left in the tin; turn out just before serving

steps.text: Melt the sugar with the water over medium heat, without stirring, until deep amber.
Pour the caramel into a 20cm round cake tin and swirl to coat the base, then heat the oven to 160C.
Whisk the condensed milk, coconut milk, eggs, vanilla and salt until smooth, then strain into the tin.
Sit the tin in a roasting dish and pour in hot water to come halfway up the sides.
Bake until just set with a slight wobble in the middle.
Lift out of the water and cool on a rack.
Chill in the fridge until firm.
Run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate with a lip to catch the caramel.

dishes.make_ahead: Make and cool the chocolate syrup up to 1 week ahead, kept in the fridge; build each glass to order so the foam holds

steps.text: Simmer the cocoa, sugar, water and salt, stirring, until smooth and glossy, then stir in the vanilla.
Cool the chocolate syrup completely.
Spoon 2 tbsp syrup into each of 4 tall glasses and add the cold milk.
Pour in the soda water in a fast stream while stirring hard with a long spoon until a thick white foam rises.
Serve straight away, with the spoon still in.

s.note: Twice-fried green plantain smashed flat, salted hot, with a sharp garlic, lime and olive oil mojo
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and cut into 3cm pieces. Heat 3cm of vegetable oil in a heavy pot to 160C and fry the pieces in batches for 4 minutes until pale gold, then lift out and smash each one flat with the base of a glass. For the mojo, crush 6 garlic cloves to a paste with 1/2 tsp salt, then stir in 80ml olive oil, the juice of 2 limes and a handful of chopped coriander. Turn the oil up to 180C and fry the smashed plantain again for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel, salt straight away and serve hot with the mojo for dipping.

s.n: Jets' corner cart hot dogs with onion sauce
s.note: Simmered frankfurts in soft rolls with a sweet, spicy tomato and onion sauce and yellow mustard
s.how: Thinly slice 2 brown onions and cook in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, a pinch of cinnamon, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp white vinegar and 125ml water and simmer for 15 minutes until thick and jammy. Simmer 8 frankfurts in barely bubbling water for 6 minutes. Warm 8 long soft rolls, tuck in the frankfurts, spread with yellow mustard and spoon over the onion sauce.

m.n: Maria's pernil with arroz con gandules
m.note: Slow-roasted pork shoulder rubbed with garlic, oregano, cumin and citrus, with sofrito rice, pigeon peas and green olives
m.how: Blend 10 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp dried oregano, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 60ml olive oil and the juice of 2 limes and 1 orange to a paste. Score the skin of a 2kg boneless pork shoulder, rub the paste all over and into the cuts, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight. Bring to room temperature, then roast skin up at 160C for 4 hours. Turn the oven to 230C for 25 minutes to crackle the skin, then rest 15 minutes. While it roasts, soften 1 chopped onion, 1 green capsicum and the coriander stalks in 2 tbsp oil, stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric and 2 cups long grain rice, then add a drained 400g tin of pigeon peas, 100g green olives and 750ml vegetable stock. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, then rest 10. Pull the pork into chunks with the crackling and serve over the rice with coriander and lime wedges.

w.note: Baked coconut and vanilla custard set over dark caramel, chilled and turned out
w.how: Melt 150g caster sugar with 3 tbsp water in a pan, without stirring, until deep amber. Pour into a 20cm round cake tin and swirl to coat the base. Heat the oven to 160C. Whisk a 395g tin of condensed milk, a 400ml tin of coconut milk, 5 eggs, 1 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt until smooth, then strain into the tin. Sit the tin in a roasting dish, pour hot water halfway up the sides and bake for 55 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool, then chill for at least 6 hours. Run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate with a lip.

d.note: Homemade chocolate syrup, cold milk and fizzing soda water, stirred hard for a white foam head
d.how: Simmer 50g cocoa, 150g caster sugar, 150ml water and a pinch of salt for 5 minutes, stirring, until glossy, then stir in 1 tsp vanilla and cool. Spoon 2 tbsp syrup into each of 4 tall glasses and add 125ml very cold milk. Pour in about 250ml cold soda water in a fast stream while stirring hard with a long spoon until a thick white foam rises to the top. Serve straight away.
